still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived. Medicare reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk codes, and Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban is still the only state ban, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. One-line arithmetic: 32.0 ever − 22.6 current = 9.4 pts used-and-off; 45.6% × 32.0 = 14.6 pts cycled = 12.4 pts current users on ≥2nd course (~55% of current) + 2.2 pts cycled and off again; the remaining 7.2 pts stopped once and never restarted. That is consistent with one-year persistence near one-third, restarts of 36–47% compounded, and 6.5 pts of new ever-users in the window. Age check: 0.20×14 + 0.33×24 + 0.24×34 + 0.23×16 = 2.8+7.92+8.16+3.68 ≈ 22.6. Income check: (30+23.5+14.3)/3 ≈ 22.6. About 22.6% of ~270M adults is ~61M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~13.8M (22.6%), Medicare ~10.8M (17.7%), Medicaid ~3.4M (5.6%), legitimate cash (TrumpRx/manufacturer direct) ~21.0M (34.4%), compounded/imported/counterfeit ~12.0M (19.7%). Sum 61.0M. Growth came mostly from people without obesity: ~8.5M users (~14%) have neither obesity nor diabetes, ~5M of them with BMI under 27, mostly top-third adults aged 35–64 on $149 starting-dose orals or compounded 'microdose' kits. 65+ growth slowed (14.5 → 16) after the fracture findings and the Sept 2031 dementia sNDA rejection. Bottom-third growth (12 → 14.3) is almost entirely gray-market. Adult obesity is ~33.2%. ~22% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third and the rural South. Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s (≈3.0% of 12–17s, ≈0.35% of 6–11s on daily liraglutide). The first cohort of 12-year-olds started in 2021–22 are now adults on their tenth year.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~10.8M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (established-CVD) codes behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 10.8M × ~$250 average net/month × 12 ≈ $32.4B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up; the dementia route (~1.8M × ~$260 × 12) ≈ $5.6B, capped at the CVD label after the Sept 2031 rejection. Medicaid ~3.4M: 9 states still cover weight-loss use at the $245 rate, and EPSDT covers some children's generic liraglutide case by case.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $5–35 a month across 90+ brands, and Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'retatrutide-type' peptide API is sold openly to compounders and peptide shops worldwide. Canadian generics run CAD 55–95. Brazil and Mexico have local generic semaglutide.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: Novo and Lilly froze TrumpRx and PBM flat-net prices at May 2029 levels (Wegovy pill maintenance $249, Foundayo $149–279, injectables $279–349, MariTide ~$299 direct). They cite serialisation and anti-counterfeit costs, retatrutide fill-finish constraints, and patent wins that keep US generics out until at least 2033. Starting oral doses stay $149, and that starting dose has become the de facto 'longevity dose' prescribed off-label by telehealth. Employer coverage moved only 36% → 35% (status quo); ~11% more cover only through monitored metabolic tracks, now ~4.8M enrollees inside the 13.8M commercial users. Gray market ~12M: ~5.5M on compounded semaglutide/tirzepatide from 503A pharmacy–telehealth networks ($99–199/month, 'metabolic microdose' kits since the June 2031 ruling), ~4M on Indian vials by mail ($30–70 landed), and ~2.5M on counterfeit pens or 'research' retatrutide and cagrilintide from social shops. Orals are ~47% of users.

GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. next_gen_launch = none, realised as: Novo's amycretin received a Complete Response Letter in Nov 2030 asking for lean-mass, bone and longer exposure data; resubmission is planned for late 2032, with no decision before 2033. No other new class was approved. Lilly filed bimagrumab + tirzepatide (muscle-preserving combination) in Apr 2032 after phase 3; the earliest decision is Apr 2033. Implant programmes remain phase 1. No oral matches tirzepatide. The tirzepatide dementia sNDA got a CRL in Sept 2031. Higher-dose retatrutide (12 mg) labelling was not expanded. US semaglutide generic entry is delayed to 2033 or later by the Mar 2031 formulation-patent ruling and prior settlements. Global incretin market ~$175B (2031). US net prices are flat in nominal terms since mid-2029.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Microdose users report less, which helps drive longevity uptake. Chronic diarrhoea is now routinely worked up for EPI.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now runs mainly on exocrine claims.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; new MDL filings cite exocrine insufficiency.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss: population-level fracture and sarcopenia burden
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The Medicare cohort holds the hip-fracture HR at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years, ~1.45 after 3+ cycles, and ~1.5 in users with BMI <30 at start. With ~6M 65+ users past two years and a baseline ~5 hip fractures per 1,000 per year: 6M × 0.005 × 0.3 ≈ 9,000 excess hip fractures a year. In a Feb 2032 claims analysis, age-adjusted hip-fracture rates among women 65+ rose for a second straight year after three decades of decline. Normal-weight longevity users lose proportionally more lean mass (~35–40% of weight lost vs ~25–30% in obesity). Sarcopenia diagnoses in users 50–64 are up roughly a third from 2029. Dementia-route and cyclers carry the highest absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning strengthened (Mar 2032): baseline and two-yearly DXA recommended for users 65+ and anyone starting with BMI <27; resistance-training and protein counselling statement extended class-wide. It weighed in the Sept 2031 dementia sNDA rejection. No restriction on prescribing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('the flats', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia still ~7–8% of users vs ~3% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. In surveys ~30% report mild 'evenness', and a majority of current users say they have skipped or stepped down a dose at least once for mood, libido or an occasion. Interim FDA observational data (2031) show dose-dependence but no RCT.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA postmarketing study continuing; no labelling.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Drug holidays of 1–3 weeks produce appetite rebound but little measurable regain. Gray-market interruptions still drive the fastest regain.
B12, iron, vitamin D, and fat-soluble vitamins in long-term and EPI users. Normal-weight microdose users show low protein intake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panels in professional guidance; label language added 2031.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: A third cohort (UK CPRD, 2031) replicated the roughly doubled EPI rate (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years) after 5+ years of semaglutide. Partial recovery of faecal elastase within 12 months of stopping in about half of cases. Tirzepatide 5-year exposure now shows a smaller, non-significant excess. It compounds bone loss via vitamin D/K malabsorption.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA added EPI to semaglutide SmPC (2031). FDA added it to semaglutide Warnings and Precautions (Aug 2031); class labelling for other incretins undecided.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up. Interim liraglutide 6–11 postmarketing data (2032) show bone-mineral accrual ~4% below matched controls at two years, with growth velocity normal; significance unclear. No data at all on decades of microdosing in normal-weight adults.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone and growth requirements continue; FDA asked for an extended adolescent bone substudy.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~26,000 by mid-2032. In Oct 2031 an endotoxin-contaminated compounded tirzepatide lot from a Florida 503A pharmacy caused 63 hospitalisations for sepsis or injection-site abscess and 1 death. Microdose kits are prone to tenfold reconstitution errors. Poison-centre calls are ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters and an import alert for peptide API from three Chinese suppliers; state boards of pharmacy inspected the Florida lot. No new federal compounding rule.

food_and_beverage.state: About 40% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~10% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. The longevity cohort (affluent, normal-weight) pushed the decline into premium categories once thought immune: craft chocolate, bakery-café pastry and wine-adjacent snacking. Protein, fibre, creatine and 'lean-mass' lines are the growth aisle. Whey prices remain elevated. Value packs and private label hold in lower-income zip codes. PepsiCo and Mondelez have restructured toward portion-pack and protein brands.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~13% from 2025 and beer ~8%. The positive AUD readout added legitimacy to EAP off-label use. Wine is now hit too, because the longevity cohort is its core buyer, and Napa and Sonoma bulk-wine prices are depressed. Non-alcoholic lines grow but don't replace margin. Bar closures continue in mid-sized Midwestern cities.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Smaller checks everywhere. 'Holiday menus' (indulgent weekend tasting menus pitched to people skipping a dose) appeared at upscale restaurants in Austin, Miami and Manhattan. Buffets keep closing. QSR value menus hold in lower-income markets.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists continue contracting. Growth is in structured athletic and 'strength' wear. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Senior-adaptive apparel (hip protectors, padded leggings) appears in mainstream catalogues.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. A new segment of 'bone and muscle clinics' for 55+ users ($150–300/month cash, DXA plus supervised loading) has spread through Florida retirement markets, e.g. The Villages and Boca Raton. Creatine is the best-selling supplement in the US. Premium clubs bundle DXA with telehealth longevity prescribing.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is ~35%, structurally unchanged. Pharmacy trend ~+6–7%. Adherence differentials persist at self-insured mid-sized firms. Part D premiums rose again for 2032, partly on incretin spend and partly on fracture and rehab claims. Medicare Advantage plans now market DXA and strength-coaching benefits. Life insurers price incretin use as neutral-to-favourable, but add DXA questions for applicants 60+.

pharma.state: Lilly, Novo, Amgen and Boehringer hold US branded share. Volume grows on longevity demand while nominal prices are frozen, so revenue growth continues. Gray-market leakage (~12M users) is now the main competitive threat, fought with lawsuits and serialisation. Lilly's bimagrumab combination is the pivot to muscle. Indian and Chinese makers dominate global volume and supply compounder API.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on a drug no longer signals anything; it is assumed. What signals is the version. A lean, muscled body reads as scanned and coached. A soft, thin body reads as cash or compounded. A regained body reads as someone who stopped, and people ask why. A frail older body with a walker after a hip fracture reads, uncomfortably, as having done everything right.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The top third now medicates without obesity. Among Austin and Charlotte professionals in their forties, a $149 starting-dose pill 'for metabolic health' is as routine as a statin was for their parents, and DXA lean-mass numbers remain the status metric. In the Columbus logistics corridor the monthly clinic shot continues. In bottom-third neighbourhoods, compounded kits from Instagram telehealths have narrowed the visible gap a little, at the cost of bad lots and abrupt stops. In Florida retirement communities, the fracture wave made bone density a dinner-table topic.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are short on weekdays and long on 'holiday' weekends, when hosts plan around guests who skipped their dose. Asking 'are you on this week?' is ordinary table manners. The Bread Alone fasting network plateaued at ~550 congregations. School cafeterias in affluent districts quietly stock protein snacks for medicated students.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list dose schedules and 'holiday weeks'. Couples schedule intimacy and celebrations around skipped doses, which is easier on weekly and oral products than on MariTide. Being off with no reason is the thing a new partner asks about. Therapists still report desire mismatch, now framed as a scheduling problem.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become something you schedule. You turn it down on weekdays and let it back for occasions. Unmedicated appetite is read as a choice that needs explaining: religious, medical, financial or political. The counter-movement is smaller and more marginal. Unmuted survives as a working-class nightlife scene, and the MAHA wing targets compounders and Chinese peptides rather than the drugs themselves.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia ~7–8% of users vs ~3% controls (~10% on retatrutide). Mild 'evenness' or 'the flats' reported by ~30%. A majority of users have taken at least one deliberate drug holiday or step-down; among cash and compounded users ~1 in 3 does so monthly.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect you manage. People call it 'the flats', telehealths sell 'holiday protocols' and 'titration for joy', and clinicians call it a dose-related adverse effect. HR's 'steadiness' language remains in metabolic-track materials, though less in marketing after the flats became a household complaint among managers themselves.
interior_life.effect_on_work: The complaint is classless and the remedy is not. Cash and compounded users skip a week before a pitch, a wedding or a vacation. The ~4.8M workers in adherence-verified tracks (monthly clinic-administered MariTide, or PBM-verified weekly fills) cannot take a holiday without losing up to a 30% premium differential, so they live with the flats or pay cash for a parallel prescription. The EEOC charges remain unresolved. Sales and creative firms informally encourage 'pitch holidays'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday weekend' is a cultural form, with tasting menus, festivals and club nights timed to skip cycles. Some promoters in Detroit and Austin run Friday-to-Sunday events for people coming off a dose. Flat fiction has become a parody genre. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in insured suburbs. Musicians openly discuss touring off-dose.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Planned intimacy around skip weeks is normal. Monthly-shot couples report more 'parallel lives' because they can't time a holiday. Libido complaints are the single most common reason for a dose step-down in telehealth intake data.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No state action. Normalisation drained energy from the anti-adherence-premium coalition. The live political issues are senior fractures and Part D premiums, raised by AARP and Florida congressional offices without legislation, and compounder safety after the Florida lot, raised by MAHA-adjacent legislators who target Chinese API. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: No new state, congressional or HHS action. The FDA works through routine channels: CRLs for amycretin and the tirzepatide dementia extension, EPI and bone label updates, warning letters to compounders. It does not curb microdose compounding after losing the June 2031 case, and has not appealed. Enforcement on imports is still porous.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new. TrumpRx operates on frozen manufacturer prices. Bridge not revived. The 2027 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Clinic administration records and PBM fills feed wellness vendors. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Telehealth longevity platforms collect DXA and wearable data under broad consent.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE unchanged. The Army oral pilot is unexpanded. DOT has still not ruled on drivers using drugs for alcohol reduction. Some fire departments added DXA to fitness-for-duty exams for older medicated firefighters.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India supplies most finished generic volume and China most peptide API, including the retatrutide-type peptide sold to US compounders and peptide shops. US–India trade talks are still unresolved on mail enforcement. The price gap between Indian generics and US cash is ~40×, unchanged because neither side moved.

events.event: FDA issues Complete Response Letter for Novo's amycretin, asking for lean-mass, bone-density and longer exposure data; Novo targets resubmission in late 2032

Delaware federal court upholds Novo's semaglutide formulation patents against generic filers, pushing US generic entry to 2033 or later; Novo and Lilly confirm TrumpRx and PBM prices will stay frozen at 2029 levels

Federal judge in Texas dismisses Lilly's suit against a telehealth-compounding network, finding sub-0.5 mg 'metabolic microdose' tirzepatide clinically different from Zepbound; within six months ~40 platforms sell $99–179 kits, many to people without obesity
FDA rejects Lilly's bid to extend tirzepatide's dementia-risk claim to adults 60+ without heart disease, citing Medicare-cohort fracture data and the unfinished confirmatory trial

Medicare claims analysis finds hip-fracture rates in women 65+ rose for a second year after three decades of decline, ~9,000 excess a year attributed to incretins; FDA strengthens class bone warning in March, and Lilly files muscle-sparing bimagrumab combination in April
KFF poll: 58% of current users have deliberately skipped or cut a dose for mood, libido or an occasion, and 64% of adults say taking an incretin is 'no different from a statin'

open_tensions: Longevity use has put millions of normal-weight adults on decades-long therapy just as normal-weight users are shown to lose proportionally more muscle and bone, and there is no long-horizon data on microdosing at all.
The compounded gray market grew to ~12M users on the strength of one court ruling and frozen brand prices. The Florida sepsis lot showed the cost, and the FDA has neither appealed nor written a rule.

Drug holidays are the normal remedy for the flats, except for the ~4.8M workers in adherence-verified tracks, where skipping a monthly clinic dose costs up to 30% in premiums. The EEOC charges are still undecided.
Lilly's bimagrumab filing and Novo's amycretin resubmission both land in 2033. Part D premiums are climbing on incretin and fracture costs, and the dementia extension is rejected but not dead.

prose.headline: Everyone's On It, Nobody Talks About It: 61 Million Americans, Frozen Prices, and the Weekend You Skip Your Dose
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 a little more than one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, about 61 million people, and nearly a third have taken one at some point. Most of the growth did not come from people with obesity. It came from people who wanted to stay as they were. In Austin, Charlotte and the suburbs of Denver, a telehealth prescription for the $149 starting dose of the Wegovy pill, taken 'for metabolic health', has become something forty-somethings mention the way their parents mentioned a statin. Being on it is unremarkable. Being off it is what people ask about.

The prices stopped falling. In March 2031 a Delaware court upheld Novo's formulation patents, and generic semaglutide will not reach American pharmacies before 2033. Novo and Lilly kept their 2029 cash prices where they were: $249 for the pill at maintenance, $279 to $349 for the pens, and the $1,349 list price still printed on a box nobody pays for. Employers didn't come back and didn't leave in any number. Barely a third cover the drugs for weight loss. Medicare still pays only through diabetes, heart, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia codes.

The cheap supply arrived through the gap that left. In June 2031 a Texas judge ruled that tiny 'microdose' tirzepatide made by compounding pharmacies was clinically different from Lilly's pens, and within months dozens of telehealth platforms were selling kits for around $129 a month. Add Indian vials by mail and Chinese 'research' peptides, and about twelve million Americans take something no regulator has inspected. In October a contaminated lot from a Florida pharmacy put sixty-three people in hospital. The kits kept shipping.

The bodies told the other story. Medicare data published in February showed that hip fractures among older women had risen for a second year, reversing a thirty-year decline, at roughly nine thousand extra fractures a year. Normal-weight users, it turns out, lose more muscle for each pound than anyone. The FDA strengthened its warning, told doctors to scan bones, and in September 2031 refused to extend Lilly's dementia-prevention claim to older people without heart disease. Lilly answered with a filing for a muscle-sparing combination that won't be decided until 2033. No new class of drug reached the market. Novo's amycretin was sent back for more bone data. In The Villages and Boca Raton, 'bone clinics' with squat racks and scanners have opened beside the pharmacies, and creatine is the best-selling supplement in the country.

What everyone talks about is the flats. The evenness that HR departments once praised as steadiness is now a common complaint at dinner parties, and the people complaining are often the managers. The remedy is just as common: skip a week. More than half of users say they have done it, before a wedding, a pitch, an anniversary. Upscale restaurants sell 'holiday menus'. Club nights in Detroit run Friday to Sunday for people coming off a dose. Couples plan around the skipped week.

Not everyone can skip. Nearly five million workers sit in employer metabolic tracks, many getting monthly shots at plant clinics outside Columbus, and a missed appointment can cost up to thirty percent of their premium. They live with the flats, or pay cash on the side. The EEOC complaints about it are still undecided, and no legislature has taken them up.

The country is thinner, calmer and a little more fragile. Snack and wine makers are rebuilding around protein. Part D premiums are rising on drug spending and on hip surgeries. Children who started on these drugs at twelve are now adults in their tenth year of treatment, and no one can yet say what thirty years will do.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Renee Castillo, fifty-eight, scrapes plaque off a stranger's molars at eight-fifteen and notices the patient's chart says tirzepatide, like most charts now. Renee's own kit is in her refrigerator at home in Brandon: four compounded microdose syringes from a telehealth called Basal, $139 a month on her debit card. Her BMI was twenty-six when she started. Her sister said it was the best thing she'd ever done for her blood sugar, and Renee's blood sugar had never been a problem, but she said it anyway.

She isn't taking this week's dose. Saturday is Hector's sixtieth, and she wants to taste the cake, want the cake, want Hector.

At lunch the other hygienist, Tasha, eats a protein bar and says she's 'on' this week because of a sinus thing, as though Renee had asked.

After work Renee drives to the rehab place on Bloomingdale. Her mother broke her hip in March, stepping off a curb at Publix. She was on Zepbound through Medicare for her heart, and the surgeon showed them the scan, the bone like lace. Her mother does her parallel-bar laps and asks whether Renee has had her own scan yet. Renee says it's booked. It isn't.

At home there's an email from Basal: a new 'Bone-Safe Protocol', creatine and vitamin D added, $40 more. She closes it.

Hector is grilling. The smell hits her harder than it has in a year, and for a second she thinks she might cry, just from the smell. She doesn't tell him. She sets two plates.

least_plausible_claims.quote: It does not curb microdose compounding after losing the June 2031 case, and has not appealed.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the June 2031 event is Lilly's private suit being dismissed, and the FDA was not a party. It cannot have 'lost' that case or failed to appeal it, so the stated reason for the FDA's inaction contradicts the world's own events.

least_plausible_claims.quote: It weighed in the Sept 2031 dementia sNDA rejection.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the sentence follows the March 2032 strengthened warning, which cannot have influenced a September 2031 decision. This is a chronology contradiction. The rejection may rest only on earlier Medicare-cohort data.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ~9,000 excess a year attributed to incretins
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the 9,000 figure comes from multiplying the 1.3 hazard ratio by a baseline rate, not from a measured national excess. Presenting it as the finding of a claims analysis that 'attributes' it to incretins asserts causation from an aggregate trend, a leap the candidate does not show.

rationale.badness: public_health: a hip-fracture wave, EPI on the label, a contaminated compounded lot and decades of microdosing in normal-weight adults with no data. autonomy and inequality: ~4.8M workers in adherence-verified tracks cannot take the 'holiday' everyone else uses to manage the flats, and cash and compounded users skip doses while the verified cannot. The harms are measured and discussable (KFF poll, claims analysis, FDA label changes), so epistemic and cohesion score lower. The result is a harder society with new losers, not a structurally hidden one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible. Adoption is +5.0pp, prices are frozen, coverage is 36→35%, longevity use is mainstream, the bone wave, gray-market growth, normalisation and the 'flats' complaint all appear, and next_gen is realised as a CRL plus a filing. The only strain is routine FDA label action against state_action none. mechanism: most chains are shown (patent ruling → frozen prices; microdose ruling → kits; fractures → label and sNDA rejection), but the FDA 'losing the case and not appealing' contradicts the events, the March 2032 warning is said to have influenced a September 2031 decision, and the 9,000 excess is attributed rather than measured. magnitude: 22.6% on drug and 32.0% ever-used are inside the envelope, the income and age checks reconcile, and the payer mix sums to 61.0M. Medicare spending (10.8M×$250×12 = $32.4B) and the cycling arithmetic also reconcile. Approval timing is respected, with no generic and bimagrumab decided no earlier than 2033. The only gap is a minor pediatric sub-band mismatch.
rationale.generativity: The prose and the Renee Castillo vignette give concrete scenes: the skipped dose before Hector's birthday, the mother's rehab laps, the Basal upsell email and the hygienist's 'sinus thing'. The world has texture (holiday menus, bone clinics in The Villages, Detroit off-dose club nights, DXA at firehouses) and implies many other characters. The vignette shows rather than explains, though 'most charts now' is hyperbole.

least_plausible_claims.quote: It does not curb microdose compounding after losing the June 2031 case, and has not appealed.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the June 2031 event is Lilly's private suit against a telehealth network, so the FDA was not a party and could not have 'lost' or appealed it. The state field contradicts the events list.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Federal judge in Texas dismisses Lilly's suit against a telehealth-compounding network, finding sub-0.5 mg 'metabolic microdose' tirzepatide clinically different from Zepbound; within six months ~40 platforms sell $99–179 kits, many to people without obesity
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a single district-court dismissal is not binding nationally, yet it is credited with building a ~5.5M-user compounded market and doubling gray-market users within about 18 months. The scaling is asserted, not shown, and FDA's non-response is unexplained.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Pediatric: ~1.4% of under-18s (≈3.0% of 12–17s, ≈0.35% of 6–11s on daily liraglutide).
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: with roughly 25M children in each of the 12–17 and 6–11 bands, those sub-band rates give about 1.15% of under-18s, not 1.4%. The pediatric figure does not reconcile with its own sub-figures.

rationale.badness: The world is harder with new losers. About 9,000 excess hip fractures a year, a fracture wave in older women, and normal-weight users losing proportionally more lean mass lower flourishing and public health. About 12M people use uninspected product, with sepsis lots and tenfold reconstitution errors, and the 4.8M workers in adherence-verified tracks cannot take the 'holiday' everyone else uses to manage the flats.
